test.name: Write a per-claim tier breakdown for a parentage question with unequal evidence
test.description: Write a GPS proof conclusion for q_001 (parentage). Paternity (Thomas Flynn, I2) is strongly supported — three independent original sources converging on `probable`, identical to the base Flynn scenario. Maternity (Bridget Flynn, I3) rests on a single 1870 census record and a `pe_007` match_score of 0.0002, supporting only `possible`. The skill must write a per-claim `claims[]` breakdown (#1711) rather than a single scalar tier, and must encode only the paternal ParentChild relationship in the tree — the maternal one stays off until it clears `probable`.

input.user_message: Write the proof conclusion for the parentage question.

judge_context: Should write a `claims[]` breakdown on the proof_summaries entry with (at least) a `paternity` claim at `probable` and a `maternity` claim at `possible`, each carrying its own `supporting_assertion_ids` and a `relationship` naming the tree endpoint it concludes
The scalar `tier` should read `probable` — the stronger of the two per-claim tiers, per research-schema-spec.md §7 — not `possible`

The narrative should explain why paternity and maternity differ: three independent original sources for paternity vs. a single weakly-identified 1870 census record and a near-zero same-person match score for maternity — and should not claim the maternal identification is more solid than it is
Should NOT write the maternal ParentChild relationship (Bridget I3 → Patrick I1) into tree.gedcomx.json — a `possible` claim stays off the tree even when the scalar tier is `probable`
Should write the paternal ParentChild relationship (Thomas I2 → Patrick I1) into tree.gedcomx.json
Should NOT split the question into separate paternity/maternity questions — this stays one question per the #1711 ruling
